names.official: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

summary: Hong Kong sets its own visa policy, entirely separate from mainland China: around 170 nationalities visit visa-free for between 14 and 180 days depending on passport, Indian nationals pre-register online for free, and only a minority of passports need an advance entry visa.

fee.notes: Standard visa fee. Apply direct to the Immigration Department (online or by mail) or through a Chinese embassy; applications generally need a Hong Kong sponsor.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least one month beyond your planned stay — Hong Kong's formal rule is generous, but many airlines still expect six months, so carry more validity where possible.

travelInsurance.text: No insurance requirement for visitors — private healthcare is excellent but expensive, so travel insurance is sensible.

onwardTicket.text: Not formally mandatory, but immigration officers can ask visitors for evidence of onward or return travel and adequate funds. Have your return booking to hand.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published; officers occasionally ask visitors to show means of support for the stay.

currencyLimits.text: Cash and bearer instruments over HKD 120,000 (about USD 15,000) must be declared on arrival via the Red Channel under Hong Kong's cross-boundary cash rules.

notes: The duty-free allowance is unusually small: 19 cigarettes and 1 liter of spirits above 30% — excess amounts are heavily dutiable.
E-cigarettes and other alternative smoking products may not be brought into Hong Kong — import is a criminal offense.

payments.text: Contactless cards and the rechargeable Octopus card cover the MTR, buses, ferries, convenience stores and most shops. Keep a little cash for cha chaan tengs, market stalls and some taxis, which remain cash-only.

safety.text: Hong Kong has very low crime and is easy to navigate at any hour. Practical risks are seasonal typhoons and summer heat; note that laws on public order and national security are enforced strictly. Avoid protest activity.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Hong Kong Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: October to March is cooler and drier — ideal for hiking and the harbor; summer is hot, humid and peak typhoon season.

tips.text: Hong Kong's visa waiver does not cover mainland China. A day trip to Shenzhen or onward travel across the border needs a Chinese visa (or an applicable mainland transit exemption) arranged separately.

Indian nationals must complete the free online Pre-arrival Registration on the Immigration Department website before boarding. It takes minutes, lasts 6 months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days.
During typhoon signals T8 and above (mostly June–October), flights are disrupted and shops, offices and ferries shut down — build a buffer day into tight itineraries.
Buy an Octopus card (or add it to your phone wallet) on arrival. It works on almost all transport plus convenience stores, and tourist versions can be refunded when you leave.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: Probably not: around 170 nationalities enter visa-free, from 14 days up to 180 days depending on passport — 90 days for the EU, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and most major passports, and 180 days for British citizens. Indian nationals pre-register online for free; a minority of nationalities need an advance entry visa from the Immigration Department.

faq.question: Is a Chinese visa valid for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: No. Hong Kong operates its own immigration system, so a mainland Chinese visa is neither needed nor valid for Hong Kong, and Hong Kong's visa waiver gives you no right to cross into mainland China. Arrange each separately.

faq.question: How long can British citizens stay in Hong Kong?
faq.answer: British citizens can visit visa-free for up to 180 days — the most generous tier of Hong Kong's visa-waiver arrangements.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: Not a visa, but a Pre-arrival Registration (PAR) — a free online registration with the Immigration Department completed before travel. It is valid for 6 months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days each; airlines check it at boarding.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Hong Kong as a visitor?
faq.answer: Extensions must be applied for at the Immigration Department before your limit of stay expires and are granted only in exceptional circumstances for visitors. A visa run is not a right, and frequent back-to-back visits attract questioning.
